query: High-entropy alloys can combine mechanical strength, wear resistance, corrosion protection, oxidation resistance, and thermal stability, while their large compositional space offers opportunities to tune degradation in harsh environments. Prior studies have largely considered wear and corrosion separately, and only a few reports address their combined action, leaving the governing behavior poorly understood. For a high-entropy alloy subjected to tribo-corrosion, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs the coupled response and why? Describe a controlled comparison that would isolate the governing cause, predict changes in total degradation and its wear and corrosion components relative to a matched baseline, state where the prediction should hold or fail, connect it to the available prior evidence, and identify a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In aqueous tribo-corrosion of Cr-containing FCC high-entropy alloys (HEAs), the coupled degradation is governed primarily by the competition between passive tribofilm repassivation kinetics and its mechanical removal rate within the sliding contact. The time-averaged coverage and continuity of a nanocrystalline mixed oxide/metal tribofilm set the synergy term: when repassivation outruns removal (high coverage), synergy is small; when removal outruns repassivation (low coverage), synergy dominates total loss.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase FCC CoCrFeNi-based HEA with ≥20 at.% Cr (no brittle intermetallics), solutionized and mirror-polished to Ra < 20 nm, chloride-bearing neutral aqueous electrolyte at room temperature.
generation.intervention: Impose intermittent sliding with controlled dwell times between passes that are equal to or greater than the alloy’s electrochemical repassivation time constant (τ_rep) measured in situ, while keeping total sliding distance, normal load, counterbody, temperature, pH, and electrolyte composition identical to a continuous-sliding baseline.
generation.conditions: Ball-on-disk in a three-electrode tribo-corrosion cell, 0.6 M NaCl, pH ~7, 22–25°C; 5 N normal load, 0.1 m/s sliding speed, 10 mm track radius, Al2O3 counterbody, open-circuit potential (no external bias); compare continuous sliding vs intermittent sliding with dwell ≥ τ_rep between identical-length passes.
generation.structural_mediator: Steady-state coverage, thickness, and fracture resistance of the mechanically mixed nanocrystalline passive tribofilm (Cr-rich oxide/hydroxide with metallic debris) within the wear track.
generation.mechanism: Sliding periodically depassivates the surface by rupturing or delaminating the tribofilm; the electrolyte drives repassivation via cation transport and oxide growth. The governing variable is the ratio R = (repassivation rate)/(mechanical removal rate). Intermittent sliding increases the fraction of time the surface spends repassivating relative to removal, raising tribofilm coverage and continuity, which lowers contact shear stress, suppresses fresh-metal exposure, and reduces the tribo-corrosion synergy. Continuous sliding lowers coverage, keeps fresh metal exposed, and increases synergy.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the continuous-sliding baseline at identical mechanical and environmental conditions: (a) Total material loss per unit sliding distance will decrease under intermittent sliding with dwell ≥ τ_rep; (b) The wear component (mechanically driven loss) within the track will decrease due to higher tribofilm coverage and lower interfacial shear; (c) The corrosion component attributed to electrochemical dissolution within the wear track will decrease because the covered fraction is higher and depassivation events are less frequent. The magnitude of decreases is expected to be monotonic with increasing dwell/τ_rep but is uncertain without system-specific kinetics; a measurable reduction is expected when dwell ≥ τ_rep.
generation.baseline: Same HEA, electrolyte, load, speed, temperature, and total sliding distance under continuous sliding at open-circuit potential, with no imposed dwell.
generation.boundary: Prediction should hold for HEAs capable of forming a protective passive film (e.g., Cr- or Al-containing) in neutral/near-neutral aerated aqueous media within the passive regime, and for contact stresses that do not cause continuous severe abrasion. It may fail: (i) in actively dissolving or de-passivating environments (strong acid, very high chloride, or imposed cathodic potentials that suppress oxide growth); (ii) at very high loads/speeds or with sharp third bodies that prevent any film persistence; (iii) for HEAs lacking sufficient passivating elements or with brittle intermetallics that fragment the film irreparably.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative effect sizes (percent reductions in total loss, wear, and corrosion components) depend on the specific alloy’s τ_rep, tribofilm mechanical properties, and contact mechanics and cannot be predicted here without experimental kinetics; in some alloys, intermittent sliding might slightly increase average corrosion current outside the track due to longer exposure times, though the in-track corrosion component is still expected to decrease if coverage increases.

falsification_experiment.design: Measure τ_rep electrochemically (current transient after a brief scratch at open circuit) for the chosen HEA in the test electrolyte. Run two tribo-corrosion series with identical total sliding distance: (A) continuous sliding; (B) intermittent sliding with programmed dwell times ≥ τ_rep between equal-length passes. Use a three-electrode setup to record synchronized current transients during sliding and dwell. After testing, quantify total volume loss by 3D profilometry, separate mechanical wear by conducting a purely mechanical control in inert or cathodic conditions to suppress dissolution, and estimate corrosion-derived loss by Faradaic integration of current during sliding within the track. Characterize tribofilm coverage/thickness by cross-sectional TEM or XPS depth profiling.
measurements: Time-resolved electrochemical current synchronized to sliding/dwell
Repassivation time constant τ_rep from scratch-repassivation transients
Total material loss volume (3D optical profilometry of wear track)
Wear component (mechanical) from cathodically protected tribotest or from dry reference under matched mechanics
Corrosion-derived material loss via Faraday’s law (integrated charge attributed to the track)
Tribofilm thickness/coverage and composition (XPS/ToF-SIMS/TEM of track)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If intermittent sliding with dwell ≥ τ_rep does not reduce the synergy term (defined as total loss − wear-only loss − corrosion-only loss) relative to the continuous baseline, despite confirmed increases in tribofilm coverage/thickness and comparable mechanical input, the hypothesis is falsified. Likewise falsified if synergy is invariant to large, verified changes in τ_rep (e.g., by potential or chemistry) at fixed mechanical removal rate.
